mainTopic: The dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about brothers who inherit when the בכור is unknown, and a new משנה about פדיון הבן when babies of two mothers get mixed up.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the גמרא's explanation of the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about brothers who inherit when no one knows which of them is the בכור. The first idea is that a Torah debt is like a מלוה על פה, which can be collected from heirs but not from purchasers. On that basis, the two תנאים would be arguing about whether 'half of five' סלעים can be given. That idea is knocked down by רבי יהודה's wording and by a ברייתא about ten זוז for each brother. So the גמרא concludes that both require a full five, and they argue about the view of רב אסי and רב פפא. A second version attaches the discussion to רבי יהודה's words 'the property became obligated'. In that version, רבי ירמיה learns a rule about a creditor and two men named יוסף בן שמעון, and רבא asks how property can owe when no person does. Then a new משנה lists cases where babies of two mothers get mixed up, and rules when the כהן receives five סלעים, ten, or nothing. The גמרא begins by asking why one כהן must return money when two כהנים do not, and שמואל's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: A Torah debt counts like an oral loan, and everyone accepts רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The obligation of פדיון הבן is not like a debt written in a שטר. It is like a מלוה על פה, and everyone agrees with רב פפא that such a loan is collected from heirs but not from purchasers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not considered like a debt written in a document. Everyone accepts the view of רב פפא, who said: an oral loan can be collected from the heirs but not from the purchasers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is laying down a shared starting point that both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה agree on. It is setting up the next step, which will show where they actually disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A debt that comes only from the Torah does not create a lien on property the way a written שטר does. So under רב פפא's rule, the כהן can collect from the half of the estate where the brothers count as heirs. He cannot collect from the half where they count as purchasers. That leaves only half of the five סלעים collectible.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a debt written in a legal document, which creates a lien on property
An oral loan, made without a document

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the brothers are literally buyers. Each brother is treated as partly an heir and partly like a purchaser of his share. That is why רב פפא's rule about purchasers matters here.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב פפא's rule (oral loan: collected from heirs, not purchasers) is a basic rule of debt collection. It is used here to explain why only half of the redemption money can be collected.

phrases.english: is not like one written in a document,
phrases.notes: A debt written in the Torah is treated like an oral loan.

phrases.aramaic: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: and everyone accepts the view of Rav Pappa,
as Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין
phrases.english: an oral loan is collected from the heirs
but it is not collected from the purchasers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an explanation of the משנה's dispute that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Torah-based debt is like an oral loan. It is collected from heirs but not from purchasers, so only the inheritance half is collectible.

steps.title: A proposed explanation of the dispute: can you give half of five
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about whether a partial payment of the five סלעים counts. רבי מאיר says only a full five counts. רבי יהודה says even part of five counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they disagree about 'five, but not half of five.' רבי מאיר holds: five, and not half of five. רבי יהודה holds: five, and even half of five.
steps.whatsHappening: Since both sides agree only half the money can be collected, the גמרא now pinpoints their real argument. The question is whether giving half of the five סלעים is meaningful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the מצוה is specifically five סלעים, so a partial two-and-a-half is worthless and the brothers are פטור. For רבי יהודה, even part of five fulfills something, so the כהן takes the two-and-a-half from the inheritance half.

keyTerms.meaning: Five (סלעים, the redemption price of a בכור)

steps.whatToRemember: In this explanation, the whole argument is about partial payment. רבי מאיר says only a complete five סלעים counts. רבי יהודה says even part of five counts.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּחָמֵשׁ וְלֹא בַּחֲצִי חָמֵשׁ קָמִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: and here they disagree about 'five, but not half of five,'
for Rabbi Meir holds:
five, and not half of five,
phrases.notes: So the brothers are exempt from the partial amount.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda holds:
five, and even half of five.
phrases.notes: So the כהן collects the two and a half סלעים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא בְּחָמֵשׁ וְלֹא בַּחֲצִי חָמֵשׁ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the shared premise of step 1 to identify the point of disagreement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to a different underlying issue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think they disagree about whether the estate is fully liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree only the inheritance half is liable. They disagree only about whether partial payment of five counts.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's wording does not fit
steps.stepSummary: If this explanation is right, רבי יהודה should have said 'the man became obligated,' not 'the property became obligated.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, when רבי יהודה says 'the property became obligated,' he should have said 'the man became obligated'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from step 2. It shows that רבי יהודה's own words in the משנה do not match it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the explanation, רבי יהודה agrees there is no lien on the property, because the purchaser half is lost. The payment comes only from the heirs, like an oral loan. That is a personal obligation, so 'נתחייבו נכסים' (the property is obligated) is the wrong way to describe it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר נִתְחַיְּיבוּ נְכָסִים,
phrases.english: If so, Rabbi Yehuda says 'the property became obligated'?
He should have said 'the man became obligated'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר נִתְחַיְּיבוּ נְכָסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי יהודה's view is based on 'even half of five' with only the inheritance half being collectible.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there is no lien on property, the obligation is personal. Then the wording 'נתחייבו נכסים' contradicts the explanation.

steps.title: A second challenge from a ברייתא about ten זוז
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: if brothers divided the estate and each has ten זוז, they are obligated; if not, they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, it was taught: רבי יהודה says, brothers who divided the estate: if there are ten זוז for this one and ten זוז for that one, they are obligated, and if not, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second difficulty: a ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה. It is setting up a question about what 'ten זוז' means. The actual problem comes out in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten זוז equals two and a half סלעים, since a סלע is four זוז. The ברייתא gives a minimum amount for the obligation. The explanation from step 2 will have trouble accounting for why any minimum is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin, a quarter of a סלע

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
brothers who divided the estate,
if there are ten zuz for this one
and ten zuz for that one, they are obligated,
and if not, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the same explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי יהודה holds 'even half of five.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא sets a minimum of ten זוז, which seems out of place if any partial amount is enough.

steps.title: What does 'ten זוז for each' mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to understand the ten זוז per brother mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'ten זוז for this one and ten זוז for that one' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to define the ברייתא's case. It is setting up the next step, where it tests one possible reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the ten זוז counts each brother's whole share or only part of it. The answer decides whether the ברייתא clashes with the explanation from step 2.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי עֲשָׂרָה זוּז לָזֶה וַעֲשָׂרָה זוּז לָזֶה?
phrases.english: What is meant by 'ten zuz for this one and ten zuz for that one'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי עֲשָׂרָה זוּז לָזֶה וַעֲשָׂרָה זוּז לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא just quoted to sharpen the challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'ten זוז' refer to each brother's total share (inheritance plus purchase), or to something else?

steps.title: If part of five is enough, why require ten
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the ten זוז includes both the inheritance half and the purchase half, and רבי יהודה holds even part of five counts. Then the minimum of ten makes no sense, since even less should obligate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means both inheritance and purchase together, and the rule is 'five and even half of five,' then why specifically ten? Even less than ten should also obligate them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first reading of the ברייתא and shows that it creates a contradiction. That makes the challenge to the explanation from step 2 clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any partial amount is enough for רבי יהודה, the כהן should collect whatever is available from the inheritance half, however small. So setting a minimum of ten זוז contradicts the idea of 'even half of five.'

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading to be tested)

steps.confusionAlert: Ten זוז is two and a half סלעים, which is half of five. Do not confuse זוז and סלעים when following the math.

phrases.english: If you say: counting both the inheritance part and the purchase part,
and the rule is five, and even half of five,
if so, why specifically ten?
Even less than ten should also apply!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא בֵּין דִּירוּשָּׁה בֵּין דְּלָקוֹחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one reading of the ברייתא from steps 4-5 and shows that it conflicts with step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ten זוז includes both halves, combined with 'even half of five.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If any portion is enough, the minimum of ten זוז is meaningless, because the כהן should take even a smaller amount.

steps.title: The ten זוז must be inheritance alone, so רבי יהודה requires a full five
steps.stepSummary: The other way to read the ברייתא is that each brother inherited ten זוז. That adds up to a full five סלעים. This proves רבי יהודה holds 'five, not half of five,' which knocks down the explanation from step 2.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it means ten זוז of inheritance for this brother and ten זוז of inheritance for that brother. Evidently, he holds that a full five is needed, not half of five!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it opened in step 5. It picks the only reading of the ברייתא that makes sense, and that reading proves רבי יהודה needs a full five סלעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that 'ten including the purchase half' cannot be right. So the ten זוז must be pure inheritance for each brother. Two brothers times ten זוז is twenty זוז, which equals exactly five סלעים. If רבי יהודה demands exactly that amount, he cannot hold that part of five is enough. That means the explanation from step 2 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A full five סלעים, not half of five

steps.confusionAlert: A סלע equals four זוז. So ten זוז per brother, times two brothers, is twenty זוז, which is exactly five סלעים. That is why this reading proves a full five is required.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious
ten zuz of inheritance for this one
and ten zuz of inheritance for that one
evidently: five and not half of five
phrases.notes: Twenty זוז in total equals five סלעים.

phrases.english: he holds!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא, עֲשָׂרָה זוּז דִּירוּשָּׁה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the either-or question. Step 6 ruled out the first reading, and this step takes the second reading and draws the decisive conclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation from step 2, that רבי יהודה holds even part of five counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires ten זוז of inheritance per brother, which is a full five סלעים. That shows רבי יהודה requires the full amount.

steps.title: Everyone requires a full five; the real argument is about רב אסי and רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the old explanation. Both תנאים agree that a full five סלעים is required. Their argument is really about the view of רב אסי and רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that a full five is required, not half of five. Here they argue about the view of רב אסי and רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a brand-new explanation of the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, because the old one was disproved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no disagreement about needing a full five סלעים. According to the explanation here, רב אסי and רב פפא hold that the inheritance share counts as only two and a half סלעים, which the כהן cannot collect. רבי מאיר follows their view. רבי יהודה disagrees and holds that all five סלעים are available for the redemption.
steps.whatToRemember: Final explanation of the first version: both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה need a full five סלעים. They argue only about whether the view of רב אסי and רב פפא applies.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
five and not half of five
and here, regarding the view of Rav Asi and Rav Pappa
they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא חָמֵשׁ וְלֹא חֲצִי חָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 7 disproved.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-framing the argument (moving the point of argument to a different issue)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought they argued about whether part of five counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both require a full five. They argue about the view of רב אסי and רב פפא.

steps.title: Another version: applying the discussion to the property clause, and asking when the father died
steps.stepSummary: Some teach this discussion on the later clause of the משנה, where רבי יהודה says 'the property became obligated.' The גמרא asks when the father died.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach this on the later clause, 'the property became obligated.' When did the father die?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the discussion, tied to a different part of the משנה. It opens with a setup question about timing, which prepares the two challenges that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing of the father's death matters. If he died after thirty days, the father himself was already obligated. If he died within thirty days, the obligation never fell on the father. The גמרא will test each possibility against the opinions in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on the latter clause
'the property became obligated'
when did the father die?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לֵיהּ אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the sugya on a different clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was the father's death before or after thirty days from the birth?

steps.title: If the father died after thirty days, רבי מאיר could not exempt them
steps.stepSummary: If the father died after thirty days, his property was already under a lien for the redemption. So how could רבי מאיר exempt the brothers once they divided it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he died after thirty days, does that mean רבי מאיר holds that if they divided, they are exempt? But the property was already under a lien for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first timing, death after thirty days, and shows it does not fit רבי מאיר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After thirty days the father became personally obligated, and his property became tied to that debt (שעבוד). Dividing the property among heirs should not cancel a lien that already exists. So רבי מאיר's ruling that division exempts them makes no sense in this case.

phrases.english: If you say that he died after thirty days
by implication Rabbi Meir holds
that when they divided, they are exempt?
But the property was already under lien for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּמִית לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the timing question.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the case as death after thirty days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lien already in place stays on the property even after division, so רבי מאיר could not exempt the brothers.

steps.title: If the father died within thirty days, why does רבי יהודה obligate them?
steps.stepSummary: If the father died within thirty days, the obligation falls on the unknown firstborn himself. Each brother can push the כהן away by saying 'I'm not the firstborn,' so why does רבי יהודה obligate them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means within thirty days. Then once they divided, why does רבי יהודה obligate them? Let the כהן go to this brother, and he will push him away, and to that brother, and he will push him away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second timing, death within thirty days, and shows it does not seem to fit רבי יהודה's opinion. The next step shows רבי ירמיה accepting רבי יהודה's ruling and learning a general rule about creditors from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Within thirty days the father never became obligated, so there is no lien on his property. The duty rests on the firstborn himself, but no one knows which brother he is. After the division, each brother can tell the כהן to prove he is the firstborn. So there should be no way to collect, which makes רבי יהודה's ruling hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him go to this one

phrases.english: Rather, within thirty days

phrases.aramaic: כִּי חָלְקוּ, אַמַּאי מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: when they divided, why does Rabbi Yehuda obligate?
Let him go to this one, and he will push him away
and to that one, and he will push him away!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים, כִּי חָלְקוּ, אַמַּאי מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 10 ruled out death after thirty days, so the גמרא tries death within thirty days and finds a new problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that the brothers are obligated even after dividing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no lien on the property, and each brother can claim he is not the firstborn. So the כהן cannot collect from either one.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה's lesson about two men with the same name
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה learns from רבי יהודה that a creditor can collect from a field even when he cannot say which of two same-named men owes him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: This teaches us something. Two men named יוסף בן שמעון lived in one city, and one bought a field from the other. A creditor can collect from that field. He can tell the buyer: 'If you are the one who owes me, I am taking your share. If your friend owes me, this field was already pledged to me before you bought it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה takes רבי יהודה's ruling, that the property is obligated even though each brother can push the כהן away, and turns it into a general rule about creditors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The creditor lent to 'יוסף בן שמעון' and does not know which one. Now one man owns the field that used to belong to the other. Whichever one is the real borrower, the field is open to collection: either it is the borrower's own property, or it was pledged to the debt before the sale. So the creditor collects either way.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches us (a lesson drawn from an earlier ruling)
Creditor, the person who is owed money
I have a claim against you, you owe me
Was pledged or under a lien

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the idea behind רבי יהודה: a debt can sit on property even when no single person can be forced to pay it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: This teaches us,
two people named Yosef ben Shimon
who lived in one city,
and one of them bought a field from the other —
a creditor collects from it,
because he can say to him:
If you are the one who owes me —
I am taking your own share,
and if your friend is the one who owes me —
the field was pledged to me before it became yours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 11 asked why רבי יהודה obligates the brothers, רבי ירמיה accepts רבי יהודה's ruling as it stands and draws a wider rule from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A creditor can collect from property even when it is unclear which of two people is the debtor, as long as the property is liable in every possible case.

steps.title: רבא: property only backs up the person
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the idea: a person's property is only a guarantor for him, so if the person cannot be made to pay, how can the property?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Think about it. A person's property is only a guarantor for him. If you cannot collect from the person himself, how can you collect from his guarantor?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the idea that property can be obligated when no individual person is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Property works like a ערב (guarantor) for its owner's debts. A guarantor only pays when the main borrower owes. Here each man can say 'it isn't me,' so no borrower can be forced to pay. That should mean the property cannot be collected either.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now consider, a person's property
is a guarantor for him (so how can you collect from the guarantor if not from the person?)

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי נִכְסוֹהִי דְּבַר אִינִישׁ אִינּוּן עָרְבִין בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's lesson and רבי יהודה's ruling behind it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that property can be obligated when no individual can be forced to pay.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Property is only a guarantor for its owner. With no liable borrower, the guarantor cannot be liable either.

steps.title: The rest follows the first version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that from here on, this second version continues exactly like the first version.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the rest is the same as the first version.
steps.whatsHappening: This is an editor's note. It tells us that after רבא's question, the discussion goes the same way as the first version taught earlier, so it does not need to be repeated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions differed only in where the discussion was attached: the earlier clause of the משנה or the later one, about the property becoming obligated. Once רבא raises his question, the back-and-forth that follows is identical to the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of it, the whole rest
The first version of the discussion

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions arrive at the same discussion. They differ only in which clause of the משנה the discussion is attached to.

phrases.english: And all the rest is like the first version.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלַּהּ כְּלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the second version by sending the reader back to the first version's continuation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second version merges back into the first. The rest of the discussion is the same.

steps.title: Two wives give birth to two boys: ten סלעים
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: two wives, each giving birth for the first time, have two boys that get mixed up. The father gives the כהן ten סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Two wives who had never given birth before each gave birth to a boy. The father gives ten סלעים to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a man whose two wives each have a first baby boy, and the babies are mixed up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though we don't know which baby belongs to which mother, each boy is definitely his own mother's firstborn. So both need פדיון הבן, five סלעים each, for a total of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, the new teaching being opened
Who had never given birth before
סלע coins; five are needed to redeem a firstborn

steps.confusionAlert: Being a firstborn for פדיון הבן depends on the mother, not the father. That is why one father can owe for two firstborns.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Two wives who had not given birth before
and they gave birth to two males —
he gives ten sela to the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֶׁלֹּא בִּכֵּרוּ וְיָלְדוּ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two mixed-up boys, each the certain firstborn of his own mother, require ten סלעים.

steps.title: One baby dies: one כהן or two
steps.stepSummary: If one boy dies within thirty days, the father gets five סלעים back if he paid one כהן. If he paid two כהנים, he cannot take anything back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died within thirty days: if the father gave everything to one כהן, the כהן must return five סלעים. If he gave to two כהנים, he cannot take the money back from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case where one baby dies before thirty days, the age when the obligation of פדיון הבן starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby who dies within thirty days never needed redemption, so one payment of five was not owed. One כהן clearly holds five extra and must return it. With two כהנים, each can say 'my five were for the living baby,' and the father cannot prove otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Within thirty days, before the redemption obligation starts
To take money out of their possession

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic money rule: whoever wants to take money away from someone else needs proof. Each כהן's possession protects him.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: If one of them died within thirty days,
if he gave it to one priest —
he must return five sela to him,
and if he gave it to two priests —
he cannot take it out of their possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case to the ten-סלעים ruling: one baby dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One כהן returns five. With two כהנים, the money stays with them because neither can be proven to hold the extra.

steps.title: Mixes with one surely-firstborn boy: five סלעים
steps.stepSummary: With a boy and a girl, or two boys and a girl, the father gives the כהן five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A boy and a girl, or two boys and a girl: the father gives five סלעים to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to mixed-up groups that include girls and rules that five סלעים are owed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a boy and a girl, there is only one boy who could need redemption, so the father pays five. With two boys and a girl, the girl could only have come before one of the boys. The other boy is surely a firstborn, so five is owed.

phrases.english: A male and a female,
or two males and a female —
he gives five sela to the priest;

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with mixes that include a girl.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one boy is certainly a firstborn, five סלעים are owed.

steps.title: Mixes where every boy may have come after a girl: nothing
steps.stepSummary: With two girls and a boy, or two boys and two girls, the כהן gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two girls and a boy, or two boys and two girls: the כהן gets nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with mixes where no boy is surely a firstborn, so nothing is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases, each mother may have had a girl first, which would mean no boy here opened his mother's womb. Since it is only a doubt, the כהן cannot demand payment from the father.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן has nothing here, no payment is owed

steps.whatToRemember: The rule for every mix in this משנה: pay only for a boy who is certainly his mother's firstborn. A boy who might have come after a girl is not paid for.

phrases.english: Two females and a male,
or two males and two females —
the priest has nothing here.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וְזָכָר, אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּשְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 17: here no boy is certainly a firstborn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If every boy might have been born after a girl, the כהן receives nothing.

steps.title: One wife had given birth before, one had not: two boys are born
steps.stepSummary: A man has two wives. One had given birth before and one had not. They give birth to two boys who get mixed up, and the father gives five סלעים to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: One wife had already given birth and one had not, and they gave birth to two boys. The father gives five סלעים to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new case: the same father, but now only one of his wives is having her first child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the wife who never gave birth before can produce a בכור. One of the two boys must be hers, so exactly one firstborn exists. That is why the father pays for one, five סלעים, even though we don't know which boy it is.

keyTerms.meaning: She had already given birth (so her next child is not a firstborn)
She had never given birth before

phrases.english: One [wife] had given birth before
and one had not given birth before,
and they gave birth to two males
he gives five sela'im to the כהן,
phrases.notes: One of them is certainly the firstborn of the first-time mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת בִּכֵּרָה וְאַחַת שֶׁלֹּא בִּכֵּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the case from two first-time wives to only one first-time wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One certain firstborn among two mixed-up boys means five סלעים must be paid.

steps.title: If one of those boys dies within thirty days, the father is exempt
steps.stepSummary: In the same case, if one boy dies before thirty days, the father pays nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died within thirty days, the father is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a twist to the previous case: one of the two boys dies within thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby who dies before thirty days does not need פדיון הבן. The boy who died might have been the real בכור, which would leave the living boy as the son of the mother who had given birth before. Because of this doubt, the כהן cannot force the father to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Within thirty days, before the obligation of redemption takes effect
Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Compare this to step 16. There, both wives were first-time mothers, so the living boy was certainly a בכור. Here only one was, so the living boy might not be a firstborn at all.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
phrases.english: If one of them died within thirty days
the father is exempt.
phrases.notes: The dead one may have been the firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a death to the case of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the dead baby might have been the בכור, the father owes nothing.

steps.title: The father dies: רבי מאיר says it depends on whether the brothers divided the estate
steps.stepSummary: If the father dies and both boys are alive, רבי מאיר says that a payment made before the estate was divided stays with the כהן. If they did not pay by then, they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father died and the sons are alive, רבי מאיר says: if they gave before dividing the property, they gave it. If not, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: Still in the same case, the משנה asks what happens if the father dies before redeeming, and brings רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same dispute as in the earlier משנה (48a), and it works the same way. As רבא explained there, the father died after thirty days and left only five סלעים. Before they divide, the whole five can be paid from the shared estate. After they divide, the brothers count as half heirs and half buyers (רב אסי), and a Torah debt is not collected from buyers (רב פפא), so a full five can no longer be collected, and they are exempt.

phrases.english: If the father died and the sons are alive,
Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נָתְנוּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָלְקוּ נָתְנוּ,
phrases.english: if they gave before they divided [the estate], they gave,
and if not, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת הָאָב וְהַבָּנִים קַיָּימִים, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new sub-case: the father dies before paying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, once the inheritance is divided the כהן can no longer collect a full five סלעים, so the brothers are exempt.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the obligation already rests on the father's property
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. The obligation to pay already became attached to the father's property, so the brothers must pay even after dividing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the property already became obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יהודה's opposing view about the case where the father died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, once the obligation began during the father's lifetime, it took hold of his assets. It is like a debt that sits on the estate itself. Dividing the inheritance does not remove it, so the heirs must pay the five סלעים from those assets.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute connects to a bigger question: does a Torah obligation to pay act like a lien on a person's property, the way a written loan document does?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
the property already became obligated,
phrases.notes: So the heirs must pay even after dividing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נִתְחַיְּיבוּ נְכָסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against רבי מאיר in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption obligation is attached to the father's assets, so the heirs must pay.

steps.title: A boy and a girl: the כהן gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: Back to one wife who had given birth before and one who had not. If they had a boy and a girl, the כהן gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A boy and a girl: the כהן gets nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to the case of step 19, but now the babies are a boy and a girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the girl belongs to the first-time mother and the boy belongs to the mother who had given birth before. If so, there is no בכור at all. Because of this doubt, there is nothing to pay.

phrases.english: [If they had] a male and a female
the כהן gets nothing.
phrases.notes: The girl may be the first-time mother's child.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה אֵין לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the dispute about the father's death to the basic case of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the girl could be the first-time mother's child, no payment is owed.

steps.title: Two men's first-time wives have two boys: each father pays five
steps.stepSummary: Two different men each have a wife giving birth for the first time. Two boys are born and get mixed up. Each father gives five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two women married to two men, neither of whom had given birth before, gave birth to two boys. This one gives five סלעים to the כהן and that one gives five סלעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new set of cases with two separate fathers instead of one father with two wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both mothers are first-time mothers, so each boy is definitely a בכור, whichever mother he belongs to. That means each father has a definite firstborn son, and each pays five סלעים.

keyTerms.meaning: This one gives and that one gives

phrases.english: Two women of two [different] men
who had not given birth before,
and they gave birth to two males
this one gives five sela'im to the כהן
and that one gives five sela'im.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֶׁל שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים שֶׁלֹּא בִּכֵּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New case: two fathers instead of one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each father has a certain בכור and pays five סלעים.

steps.title: One boy dies: one כהן must return five, but two כהנים keep the money
steps.stepSummary: If one boy dies within thirty days and both fathers paid the same כהן, he returns five סלעים. If they paid two different כהנים, neither can be forced to return anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died within thirty days: if they gave to one כהן, he returns five סלעים to them. If they gave to two כהנים, they cannot take it out of their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds the death of one baby to the two-fathers case and explains when money comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one living firstborn needs redemption now, so only five סלעים were truly owed. A single כהן holding ten obviously has five too many, so he gives them back. With two כהנים, each one can say, "The money I got was for the boy who lived." Nobody can prove otherwise, so the money stays with them.

keyTerms.meaning: To take [money] out of their possession

phrases.english: If one of them died within thirty [days]
if they gave to one כהן,
he returns five sela'im to them.
If they gave to two כהנים
they cannot take it out of their hands.
phrases.notes: Each כהן can claim his money was for the living child.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a death to the case of step 24. It parallels step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money comes back only when it is clear that a specific כהן holds extra. Otherwise it stays with whoever holds it.

steps.title: Two fathers with a boy and a girl: fathers exempt, the son redeems himself
steps.stepSummary: If the two first-time wives had a boy and a girl, neither father pays. The boy himself must redeem himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: A boy and a girl: the fathers are exempt, and the son is obligated to redeem himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the two-fathers case where the babies are a boy and a girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each father can say, "Maybe my child is the girl." So neither one can be made to pay. But the boy is certainly a בכור, since both mothers were first-timers, so the obligation falls on him to redeem himself when he grows up.
steps.confusionAlert: The obligation did not disappear here. It moved from the fathers to the son, because the son is definitely a בכור. We just don't know whose son he is.

phrases.english: A male and a female
the fathers are exempt,
phrases.notes: Each father can claim his child is the girl.

phrases.english: and the son is obligated to redeem himself;

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה הָאָבוֹת פְּטוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the babies in the two-fathers case to a boy and a girl.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the fathers are in doubt but the boy is certainly a בכור, the boy must redeem himself.

steps.title: Two girls and a boy, or two girls and two boys: the כהן gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: If there were two girls and a boy, or two girls and two boys, the כהן gets nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two girls and a boy, or two girls and two boys: the כהן gets nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes this section with cases where even the boy might not be a firstborn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With extra girls, it is possible that a girl was born first to each mother (with two girls and one boy, one mother had only a girl, and the other had a girl and then the boy). If so, no boy is the פטר רחם, the first to open the womb. Since nobody is certainly a בכור, neither the fathers nor the sons owe anything.

keyTerms.meaning: The first to open the womb, which is what makes a child a בכור

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern of the whole משנה: the כהן collects only when a בכור certainly exists and it is clear who owes the money. Any real doubt, whether about which child died, who the father is, or whether a girl was born first, frees the payer, because the כהן is the one trying to take money.

phrases.english: Two females and a male,
or two females and two males
the כהן has nothing here.
phrases.notes: A girl may have been born first to each mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי נְקֵבוֹת וְזָכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds girls to the case of step 26, which removes even the son's certain status as a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a girl may have been born first to each mother, there is no definite בכור and no payment.

steps.title: Two men, one wife had given birth before, two boys born
steps.stepSummary: Two men each have a wife. One wife had given birth before and one had not. They give birth to two boys who get mixed up. The husband whose wife never gave birth before pays five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one woman had given birth before and one had not, and they belong to two different men, and they gave birth to two boys, the man whose wife had not given birth before gives five סלעים to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new mix-up case. This time the two wives belong to two different husbands, and two boys are born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both babies are boys, each husband surely has one of them. The wife who never gave birth before surely had a firstborn boy. So her husband definitely owes פדיון הבן. The other wife already had a child, so her boy is not a בכור for this מצוה, and her husband owes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Five silver coins, the payment for redeeming a firstborn son
Who had not given birth before

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the boys' mix-up creates a doubt here. It does not matter which boy is which. Each father has one boy, so the first-time mother's husband surely has a firstborn son.

phrases.english: One had given birth before and one had not given birth before,
belonging to two different men,
and they gave birth to two boys,
phrases.notes: The boys were then mixed up.

phrases.english: this man, whose wife had not given birth before,
gives five סלעים to the כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת בִּכֵּרָה וְאַחַת שֶׁלֹּא בִּכֵּרָה, שֶׁל שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of mix-up cases, now with two husbands and one wife who gave birth before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two boys, the husband of the first-time mother pays five סלעים.

steps.title: Same case, but a boy and a girl were born
steps.stepSummary: In the same setup, if a boy and a girl are born, the כהן gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a boy and a girl were born, the כהן gets nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה changes one detail: now the babies are a boy and a girl. The ruling is that nobody pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the girl belongs to the first-time mother, and the boy belongs to the woman who already gave birth. In that case there is no firstborn boy at all. The first-time mother's husband can claim that his child is the girl, and the other husband never owes, so the כהן cannot collect from anyone.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule in all these mix-up cases: the כהן collects only when a father surely has a firstborn boy. If there is real doubt, the כהן gets nothing.

phrases.english: If a boy and a girl were born,
the כהן gets nothing here.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same case as step 28, but with a boy and a girl instead of two boys.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a boy and a girl, there is doubt whether any firstborn boy exists, so the כהן gets nothing.

steps.title: Why can two כהנים refuse to return the money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. It looks back at the case of two כהנים (step 25) and explains why neither has to return money: each one can push the father away.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about two כהנים? There, the father goes to this כהן and he pushes him away, and goes to that כהן and he pushes him away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining the משנה's ruling about two כהנים. This is a setup: the next step will use this same reasoning to challenge the ruling about one כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25, two fathers paid two different כהנים, and then one boy died. Each כהן can say, 'The money I got was for the boy who is still alive.' So a father cannot prove to either כהן that his money must come back.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
He pushes him away, he refuses him

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is different about two כהנים,
that the father goes to this כהן and he pushes him away,
phrases.notes: The כהן says: I took money for the living boy.

phrases.english: and he goes to that כהן and he pushes him away?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא שְׁנֵי כֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Jumps back from the end of the משנה to the earlier ruling about one כהן versus two כהנים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes the two-כהנים case different, so that no money is returned?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each כהן can push the father away by claiming his money was for the living boy.

steps.title: One כהן should be able to push both fathers away too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the same argument works for one כהן. He can tell each father 'your son is the living one.' So why must he return five סלעים? שמואל is introduced to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: With one כהן too, let the father go to him and let him push him away, and let the other father go to him and let him push him away! שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling from step 25 that one כהן must return five סלעים. The step ends by introducing שמואל, whose answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one כהן received both payments and one boy died, he could tell each father separately, 'Your son is alive, so I keep your money.' This is the same pushing-away logic used for two כהנים. So why does the משנה make him return money?
steps.confusionAlert: It seems obvious that the one כהן holds five extra סלעים, since he got both payments. But each father alone cannot prove the dead boy was his, so the כהן could still push away each father one at a time. Wait for שמואל's answer on the next amud.

phrases.english: With one כהן also,
let this father go to him and let him push him away,
phrases.notes: The כהן says: your son is the one still alive.

phrases.english: and let that father go to him and let him push him away!
שמואל said:
phrases.notes: Introduces the answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן אֶחָד נָמֵי לֵיזִיל לְגַבֵּי הַאי וְלִידַחֲיֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reasoning from step 30 and applies it to the one-כהן case to challenge the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling (step 25) that one כהן must return five סלעים when one boy dies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pushing-away argument that protects two כהנים should also let one כהן refuse each father separately.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up שמואל's answer on the next amud: the משנה's one-כהן case is where one father comes with a הרשאה (authorization) from the other, so the כהן cannot push him away.
